description: We are developing Liwa Smart Farms, an innovative smart agriculture project supporting date-palm farmers in Liwa, Abu Dhabi. details:
Liwa Smart Farms – Grow Smarter, Save Every Drop

What does the project do?

Liwa Smart Farms is a smart agriculture and farm-management prototype designed to support date-palm farmers in Liwa, Abu Dhabi. It brings environmental information and digital tools together in one accessible platform.

The system retrieves regional environmental data from NASA POWER, including air temperature, relative humidity, precipitation, and solar radiation. This information is displayed through an interactive web dashboard to help users understand environmental conditions that may affect farm-management decisions.

The platform also includes AI-assisted leaf screening, a voice-enabled farmer assistant, warning notifications, email alerts, and a cost-planning calculator. An ESP32 touchscreen demonstrates how selected dashboard information can be displayed on a physical device.

How does it work?

NASA POWER data is retrieved and presented through the web dashboard. Users can review environmental indicators, explore the available assistance tools, and view alerts and planning information. The ESP32 demonstration connects the digital platform with a physical display.

The leaf-screening feature provides an AI-assisted visual indication only; it is not a validated plant-disease diagnosis. The platform is a decision-support prototype and does not independently control irrigation.

Benefits and intended impact

The project aims to make environmental information easier for date-palm farmers to understand and use. It promotes awareness of water and energy resources, supports better planning, and encourages more sustainable agricultural practices.

Our intended impact is to help farmers make more informed decisions, identify areas that may need attention, and explore opportunities to reduce resource waste. Future development will include local soil-moisture and pump-energy sensors, field testing, and feedback from date-palm farmers.

Tools and technologies

  • NASA POWER API for regional environmental data
  • Python for the web server and data handling
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the web interface
  • ESP32 development board with a touchscreen display
  • Arduino IDE and C++ for the ESP32 demonstration
  • AI-assisted tools for development support and prototype features
  • GitHub for source-code hosting
  • Render for public web deployment

What makes the project creative?

The creativity lies in integrating NASA environmental data, AI-assisted features, a farmer-focused web dashboard, alerts, cost planning, and an affordable ESP32 hardware demonstration into one platform for a specific agricultural context: date-palm farming in Liwa.

Rather than presenting environmental data as numbers alone, the project aims to make it more accessible and relevant to farm-management decisions.

Factors considered

The project considers the needs of date-palm farmers, accessibility, water and energy awareness, the regional agricultural environment, affordability, and the possibility of future expansion. We also considered the limitations of regional satellite-derived data: it cannot replace measurements taken directly from an individual farm.
